key_insight: A drilled-to-bossed joint geometry combined with optimized DDFW parameters substantially improves AA2024-T351 weld strength, while deep learning can predict tensile performance from process settings.
engineering_relevance: The study offers a practical route to stronger lightweight aluminum joints for aerospace and automotive assemblies by pairing geometry-driven mechanical interlocking with data-driven process optimization.
method: Used an L18 orthogonal array to test friction pressure, forging pressure, spindle speed, joint geometry, and friction time.
Compared conventional flat-to-flat joints against a novel drilled-to-bossed geometry inspired by mortise-and-tenon design.
Trained deep learning models, including an ensemble residual network, to predict ultimate tensile strength from welding conditions.
evidence_signal: The best condition achieved 538 MPa tensile strength and 325 MPa torsional strength, and the top prediction model reached about R² = 0.81.
watch_item: The reported predictive accuracy is moderate, so broader validation on more datasets and operating conditions would be needed before deployment.
paper_title: Enhancing weld performance of AA2024-T351 using drilled-to-bossed geometry and deep learning prediction in direct drive friction welding
